$comment: WHAT plays and HOW LOUD. The cue sheet owns WHEN. Six roles, each naming the files it may use, how the film should line them up, how loud they sit, and how far they pull the music down. Written by hand from measurements (tools/rate-draw.mjs, tools/mask-check.mjs) and reviewed in docs/decisions.md D12 — every number here has a reason recorded there. Roles resolve against the ACTIVE sfx set in src/data/sfx.json; a set that lacks a file named here fails `npm run verify:assets`.
$anchorNote: anchor 'start' schedules the file at the action instant; anchor 'attack' schedules it at (action - alignOffsetSec) so the sound's first strong onset lands ON the action. Per-cue alignOffsetSec lives in sfx.json and is measured, not typed.
$duckNote: duckDb is how far the MUSIC is pulled down under this role. Overlapping ducks take the DEEPEST value, never the sum: two clicks 80ms apart must not dig a 6 dB hole. attack/hold/release are seconds.
$gainNote: gainDb is relative to the cue as stored (every cue is normalised to -3 dBFS peak). `perMusic` overrides the base where a take's spectrum demands it — see D12: bed A is ~20 dB darker than bed B above 10 kHz, so one setting cannot serve both.

draw.desc: The plan drawing itself out, stroke by stroke. Plays as one continuous bed under the whole drawing beat.

B-daylight-forward.$why: Shelf deepened from -7 to -9 after re-checking against the B edit's REAL draw windows. B's 15s cut draws at 5.66-9.40s, early in the take where the bed is ~4 dB quieter at 6.3 kHz than it is later, so the -7 setting left the cue 1.4 dB OVER the music there. At -9 the worst band across all four cuts is parity (-0.1 dB at 6.3 kHz on the 15s) and everything else clears by 3-12 dB.

draw.$why: Not ducked. Every other role is a transient that borrows a moment from the music; this one runs for seconds, and a duck that long is a hole rather than a gesture. Its space is carved with EQ instead — see perMusic.

loop.$why: The base take is 7.69s and B's draw beats run to 24.33s on the 120s cut, so it has to repeat. An equal-power crossfade of a quarter second hides the seam: draw-b is a dense continuous texture with no strong transient at either end, which is exactly the material a loop works on — it is also the reason draw-a could not have been looped, since its 0.70s gaps would have landed at the seam.

bandTick.$why: For the scenes agent's 'one base + a tick on each band downbeat'. 6 dB below the base so it reads as punctuation inside the texture rather than as a separate click, and unducked: it is part of the drawing bed, and ducking the music once per bar for the length of a draw beat would pump.

type.desc: The brief being typed into the composer. Four clusters, rotated so a long run never repeats a cluster back to back.
type.$whenNote: ⚠ FOR THE CUE SHEET. These are CLUSTERS, not single keys: each file already contains 4-7 keystrokes and runs 1.36-1.92s, where the synthesised `key-*` cues they replace were single presses of ~0.07s. Firing one per typed character — which is correct for the synth set — stacks 5-7 of these on top of each other and verify:audio reports 261 `too-dense` violations across the four cuts. Fire ONE cue per cluster, no closer together than minGapSec, and let `coversKeystrokes` say how much typing each one accounts for.

click.desc: A control being used. `click` for a button, `tick` for a slider step, `chip` for selecting an option.

move.desc: A panel, card or menu arriving or leaving.

appear.desc: Something landing: a card, a review pin, the drafting sheet, a saved toast, a rendering resolving.

end.$why: Suppressed when the end card lands within 250 ms of the music's own final hit, rather than the 120 ms a strict collision test would use. Measured: version A's 60s cut puts them 200 ms apart and its 120s cut 160 ms apart. Both clear 120 ms and both are a flam — two impacts that close read as a stumble, not as two events, and the music's resolution is the better of the two. So on those cuts the music finishes the film alone.
end.$tailNote: The end cue is capped at 1.8s in the prompt bank because the end card leaves about 2.0s of film after it on the tightest cuts. The 3.0s take ran 0.94s past the master on both the 30s and the 120s. The impact is at t=0, so the cap costs ring-out and not the event.

$measured.$bedFinalHitNote: Where each bed's own last strong hit lands, measured by tools/lib/dsp.mjs findEnding(). The `end` role's suppression rule reads these. A beds resolve 4.0s before the end, B beds 2.45s before.
$measured.$note: bedFinalHitSec is MEASURED from the delivered beds by tools/measure-bed-hits.mjs; `--check` fails on drift. The endcard side is deliberately NOT cached here — it comes from timeline.endcardStartSec(cut, aspect) per version, because the edit is still changing.
